title: Smoke has no boundary: binary smoke masks are annotation artifacts whose variance exceeds model differences.
problem: Known: smoke segmentation datasets (SMOKE5K, SmokeSeg) provide binary masks over a physically continuous opacity field; inter-annotator boundary variance for faint smoke is unmeasured.
hypothesis: Inter-annotator IoU on faint-smoke regions is lower than the IoU differences separating published methods, i.e., current leaderboard orderings on smoke segmentation are statistically meaningless in the faint regime that matters for early detection.
why_important: Early-warning value lives exactly in the faint regime; if evaluation there is noise, the field is optimizing nothing.
why_novel: Multi-annotator agreement studies exist for medical images, never for smoke; the leaderboard-invalidity implication is unstated in the smoke literature.
minimal_experiment: Re-annotate 200 SMOKE5K test images with 4 independent annotators; stratify agreement by opacity proxy (local contrast); compare inter-annotator IoU spread with method-gap distribution from reproduced baselines.
main_risk: Annotator recruitment/training; opacity proxy imperfect without transmission GT.
survival_note: Foundational for the whole smoke subtheme; do first.

title: Opacity regression transfers from synthetic to real smoke better than binary masks do.
problem: Known: SMOKE5K mixes synthetic (with compositing-derived alpha available in principle) and real data; models are trained on binarized targets, discarding the physically meaningful alpha.
hypothesis: Models trained on synthetic alpha-matte (opacity) targets and binarized only at evaluation transfer to real smoke with a smaller syn-to-real gap than models trained directly on binary masks, because opacity is the physically stable quantity across rendering and reality.
why_important: Would reframe smoke segmentation as matting/density estimation, changing dataset design and evaluation for the field.
why_novel: Transmission-guidance has appeared as an auxiliary signal (known); the syn-to-real transfer comparison of target parameterizations has not been run.
minimal_experiment: Recover alpha for SMOKE5K synthetic subset (or re-composite from source assets/SYN70K-style pipelines); train matched models on alpha vs binary targets; evaluate both on real test split binarized at multiple thresholds.
main_risk: Alpha recovery for existing composites may be impossible; may need re-rendering, adding cost.
survival_note: Strong; concrete reframing with clear test.

title: Fire is emissive, not reflective: segmentation failure conditioned on exposure and sensor saturation.
problem: Known: segmentation models implicitly assume reflective photometry (appearance from illumination x albedo); flames are light sources that saturate sensors and bloom, violating the assumption in ways nobody quantifies.
hypothesis: Fire segmentation error is dominated by exposure-dependent factors (saturation fraction, bloom radius) rather than semantic confusion: the same fire under bracketed exposures yields wildly different masks, and models rank-order scenes by exposure, not by fire extent.
why_important: Surveillance cameras auto-expose; if masks are exposure-artifacts, downstream fire-size estimation is unreliable in exactly the large-fire cases that matter.
why_novel: Exposure bracketing as a controlled probe for emissive-object segmentation has not been used; fire datasets have no exposure metadata analysis.
minimal_experiment: Collect small bracketed-exposure fire/flame video set (controlled burns, public HDR fire footage); run existing models per exposure; quantify mask instability vs saturation statistics; supplement with synthetic HDR renderings.
main_risk: New data collection needed; safety/logistics for controlled burns - synthetic arm mitigates.
datasets: D-Fire, FASDD, FLAME (public) + small new HDR captures
survival_note: Keep; physics-grounded critique with practical stakes.

title: Irreducible ambiguity of transparent objects in RGB: same-object different-background captures give an aleatoric floor.
problem: Known: transparent object appearance is mostly inherited from background (Trans10K literature acknowledges this); no one has measured the aleatoric error floor this implies for single-image RGB segmentation.
hypothesis: For matched transparent objects photographed against varied backgrounds, even human observers and oracle-finetuned models exhibit a background-dependent error floor: a quantifiable fraction of glass extent is fundamentally undecidable from single RGB, bounding all future methods.
why_important: Establishes what performance claims are physically credible on Trans10K-style benchmarks and justifies multi-cue (polarization/depth/motion) sensing with a number, not a vibe.
why_novel: Everyone says transparency is hard; nobody has isolated an information-theoretic floor via controlled same-object multi-background capture.
minimal_experiment: Capture ~30 glass objects x 20 backgrounds rig; measure human annotation agreement and best-model accuracy per background; decompose error into object-driven vs background-driven variance components.
main_risk: Lab captures may not represent wild scenes; complement with Trans10K subsets of repeated object instances if identifiable.
datasets: New small capture set; Trans10K, GDD, GSD (public) for context
survival_note: Strong; produces a reusable floor estimate for the subfield.

title: Glass segmentation models detect frames, not glass: counterfactual frame-removal quantifies the context crutch.
problem: Known: glass surfaces are usually delimited by frames/mullions; models may localize the frame pattern rather than perceiving transparency.
hypothesis: Inpainting/removing frames while preserving the glass region collapses glass-detection accuracy by more than half of its margin over trivial baselines, demonstrating that current 'glass perception' is mostly frame detection; frameless glass (glass walls, curved vitrines) accuracy approaches chance.
why_important: Frameless glass is precisely the safety case (people and robots walk into it); benchmark scores driven by frames give false confidence.
why_novel: Context reliance is suspected in the glass literature; a causal frame-ablation experiment has not been published.
minimal_experiment: On GDD/GSD/Trans10K, segment frames via annotation; create frame-inpainted counterfactuals with manual QC; evaluate models before/after; additionally test on a small curated frameless-glass set.
main_risk: Inpainting quality; sham-inpainting control on non-frame regions required (design mirrors 0371).
survival_note: Strong; clean causal design, safety narrative.

title: Smoke-versus-fog/cloud confusion is unmeasured because datasets contain almost no hard negatives: build and test the confuser taxonomy.
problem: Known: smoke datasets contain smoke; fog, low cloud, dust, steam, and haze appear mostly as backgrounds, not as labeled hard negatives, so false-alarm behavior is uncharacterized.
hypothesis: State-of-art smoke segmentation models fire on matched fog/steam/dust imagery at rates far exceeding their reported false-positive statistics, and confusion is stratified by confuser type in a stable way (steam > fog > dust > cloud), defining an exploitable difficulty ordering.
why_important: False alarms are the deployment killer for wildfire early-warning networks; a confuser benchmark is the missing acceptance test.
why_novel: No public smoke work systematically evaluates on labeled confuser sets; the taxonomy and ordering are unmeasured.
minimal_experiment: Assemble confuser probe set from existing sources (fog: Foggy Zurich/ACDC-fog frames; steam: industrial footage; dust: agricultural footage) with 'no smoke' verification; run 5 smoke models; report per-confuser firing rates.
main_risk: Verifying true absence of smoke in wild footage; scene-content mismatch with training distributions could exaggerate rates - use matched-scene controls.
datasets: SMOKE5K models; ACDC-fog, Foggy Zurich, curated steam/dust clips (public/curated)
survival_note: Keep; immediately useful acceptance test for deployments.

title: Motion contributes more than color to human and machine smoke discrimination: a single-frame vs motion-cue decomposition.
problem: Known: smoke is turbulent and evolving; fog/cloud are quasi-static; most smoke segmentation is single-frame, implicitly betting that appearance suffices.
hypothesis: Both humans and models discriminate smoke from confusers far better with short clips than stills at matched resolution, and the machine gain from naive temporal input (frame stacking) captures only a small share of the human motion benefit - quantifying an unexploited cue.
why_important: If motion is the dominant cue, the field's single-frame benchmark culture is misdirected; camera networks already have video.
why_novel: The human-vs-model motion-benefit comparison for smoke has not been quantified; it bounds the value of temporal modeling before anyone builds it.
minimal_experiment: Psychophysics-style still-vs-clip discrimination test with human raters on matched smoke/confuser stimuli; parallel evaluation of single-frame vs frame-stacked models; compare benefit ratios.
main_risk: Stimulus curation must equate difficulty across conditions; human study logistics.
survival_note: Keep; cheap human study, decisive cue-value estimate.

title: Compression, not model capacity, is the binding constraint for distant early-smoke detection.
problem: Known: wildfire camera networks transmit compressed video; incipient smoke plumes occupy few pixels with subtle texture that codecs are designed to discard.
hypothesis: At realistic bitrates, H.264/H.265 compression removes the discriminative signal of sub-20-pixel smoke plumes such that even oracle-finetuned models on compressed data cannot recover detection performance achievable on raw frames - i.e., the bottleneck is upstream of ML. (Speculation: modern learned codecs may preserve the signal better.)
why_important: Would shift investment from model research to camera/codec configuration for early-warning networks - an infrastructure conclusion ML papers cannot see.
why_novel: Compression robustness is studied generically; the early-smoke-specific rate-distortion-detection analysis is absent.
minimal_experiment: Take high-quality wildfire-camera footage with verified first-smoke times (FIgLib-style); re-encode across bitrate ladders; train/evaluate detectors per rung; locate the bitrate knee vs plume size.
main_risk: Raw/lightly-compressed source footage with verified events is limited; partner data may be needed.
survival_note: Strong; infrastructure-level conclusion with clear experiment.

title: Translucent tissue segmentation in surgical video is an unformulated task: feasibility and annotation-consistency study for fascia and peritoneum.
problem: Known: surgical scene segmentation datasets (CholecSeg8k, EndoVis) label opaque anatomy and instruments; translucent layers (fascia, peritoneum, adhesions) that surgeons actually navigate by are unlabeled, possibly because annotation consistency is assumed impossible.
hypothesis: With a layered annotation protocol (visible-through-tissue labeling), inter-annotator consistency on translucent structures reaches usable levels (IoU > 0.5) on a nontrivial fraction of frames, establishing task feasibility and exposing where the concept is genuinely ill-posed.
why_important: Dissection-plane identification is the core of surgical skill; if the task is annotatable, it unlocks surgical guidance research; if not, that negative result stops premature product claims.
why_novel: No public dataset or annotation-feasibility study exists for translucent surgical layers.
minimal_experiment: Sample 300 frames from Cholec80/EndoVis videos; design layered annotation protocol with surgeon input; 3 annotators; report agreement stratified by tissue type and visibility conditions.
main_risk: Needs surgical annotator time (expensive); concept may fragment by procedure type.
survival_note: High-upside task-creation idea; clinical partner required.

title: Depth-sensor failure patterns are the strongest transparent-object cue: holes as signal, not noise.
problem: Known: structured-light/ToF depth returns invalid or wrong values on glass (documented in ClearGrasp/TransCG); pipelines treat depth holes as corruption to inpaint before perception.
hypothesis: A model given only the depth-invalidity pattern (binary hole mask + local statistics), with no RGB, localizes transparent objects with accuracy competitive to RGB-only models on tabletop scenes - the sensor's failure mode is itself a high-SNR transparency detector.
why_important: Reverses the standard pipeline (fix depth, then perceive) into (read the failure); zero extra sensor cost for robotics.
why_novel: Depth holes are used as auxiliary features occasionally; the holes-only sufficiency test that isolates their information content has not been run.
minimal_experiment: On TransCG/ClearGrasp/TROSD real captures, train hole-pattern-only segmenters; compare against RGB-only and RGB-D baselines; analyze which hole statistics carry the signal.
main_risk: Hole patterns are sensor-specific; cross-sensor transfer must be reported honestly.
survival_note: Strong; elegant sufficiency experiment, robotics-relevant.

title: Mirror detectors read frames and symmetry, not reflection semantics: content-swap counterfactuals.
problem: Known: mirror segmentation models (MSD/PMD benchmarks) achieve strong numbers; the hypothesized mechanism (detecting reflected-content consistency with the scene) has never been causally tested.
hypothesis: Replacing mirror interior content with plausible non-reflection imagery (window-like view, poster) leaves model predictions largely unchanged, while humans immediately reclassify - models never learned reflection reasoning, only enclosure statistics.
why_important: Mirror-vs-doorway confusion is a real robot-navigation hazard; knowing the mechanism gap prevents false safety confidence.
why_novel: Content-swap counterfactuals have not been applied to mirror segmentation; mechanism testing is absent from this literature.
minimal_experiment: Composite content-swapped variants of 200 MSD/PMD test images (manual QC); evaluate 4 mirror-segmentation models and human raters; compare prediction-change distributions.
main_risk: Compositing artifacts; requires photometric harmonization and sham-composite controls.
survival_note: Keep; falsifies a mechanism claim cleanly.

title: Center bias and contextual priors inflate camouflaged-object benchmarks: spatial-prior-only baselines on COD10K.
problem: Known: camouflaged object detection (COD) benchmarks (COD10K, CAMO, NC4K) show rapid 'progress'; photographic conventions (centered, scale-normalized subjects) may leak object location independently of camouflage-breaking ability.
hypothesis: A blind spatial-prior model (trained only on GT mask statistics, never seeing images) plus a generic saliency model captures a large fraction of reported COD performance, and model-vs-prior margins shrink further on decentered crops - much of COD progress is dataset composition, not camouflage perception.
why_important: COD is pitched for search-and-rescue and medical analogies; if benchmarks reward photographic bias, transfer claims are hollow.
why_novel: Center-bias critiques exist for saliency; the COD field has not run its trivial-baseline audit.
minimal_experiment: Fit position/scale prior from COD10K training masks; evaluate prior-only and prior+saliency baselines on test sets; re-evaluate SOTA models on decentering/rescaling perturbations.
main_risk: Decentering crops change context realism; report both cropped and padded variants.
survival_note: Cheap audit with high corrective value; do early.
suspected_published: possibly - bias audits common elsewhere; COD-specific prior baseline seems unpublished

title: Multi-hypothesis evaluation for ambiguous boundaries: single-mask metrics rank camouflage models inversely to human preference in ambiguous regions.
problem: Known: camouflage/smoke/infiltrative-lesion boundaries admit multiple defensible delineations; benchmarks score against one mask, penalizing models that express plausible alternatives.
hypothesis: When multiple valid reference hypotheses are collected for ambiguous COD cases, model rankings under best-hypothesis matching differ substantially from single-GT rankings, and the multi-hypothesis ranking correlates better with human expert preference.
why_important: Would demonstrate that a chunk of leaderboard ordering in ambiguous-object tasks is reference-choice artifact, motivating distribution-valued ground truth.
why_novel: Multi-rater evaluation exists in medical; porting the multi-hypothesis critique with preference validation to COD/smoke is new.
minimal_experiment: Collect 3-5 independent annotations for 150 ambiguous COD10K/CAMO cases; re-rank 8 published models under single vs multi-hypothesis metrics; run pairwise human preference on disagreement cases.
main_risk: Annotation cost; ambiguity case selection must be pre-registered to avoid cherry-picking.
survival_note: Strong; links B3 to evaluation cluster B11.

title: Smoke masks should predict visibility: a transmissometer-grounded external validity test for smoke segmentation.
problem: Known: smoke segmentation is evaluated by mask overlap; the physical quantity of interest downstream (visibility reduction, optical density) is never validated against instruments.
hypothesis: Predicted smoke masks (and their soft variants) correlate only weakly with instrument-measured optical density along sight lines, and simple photometric transmission estimates outperform learned masks as visibility predictors - segmentation as practiced does not measure smoke.
why_important: Fire-safety engineering consumes visibility, not IoU; the external-validity gap determines whether this literature connects to its stated application.
why_novel: No published link between smoke segmentation outputs and physical transmission measurements exists.
minimal_experiment: Use smoke-chamber or controlled-burn footage with co-located transmissometer/opacity-meter readings (fire-research archives, e.g., NIST fire data); regress instrument readings on mask statistics vs photometric baselines.
main_risk: Instrumented footage access; NIST fire test archives may need scraping and alignment effort.
datasets: NIST fire research data, controlled-burn archives (public); SMOKE5K models
survival_note: High-concept external-validity study; keep if instrumented data located.

title: A specular-vs-transparent-vs-translucent confusion taxonomy: models collapse three physically distinct phenomena into one texture class.
problem: Known: glossy opaque, transparent refractive, and translucent scattering surfaces produce related but physically distinct image statistics; datasets label them under coarse classes (glass, mirror) without physical grounding.
hypothesis: Models trained on Trans10K/GDD/MSD confuse the three physical categories at high rates on a physically labeled probe set, and their errors track surface gloss statistics rather than transmission properties - the learned concept is 'shiny stuff', not light transport.
why_important: Robotic interaction differs radically across the three (grasp through, avoid, or ignore); collapsing them is an action-relevant failure.
why_novel: No physically-grounded confusion analysis exists across these categories; requires a probe set with measured/known material properties.
minimal_experiment: Assemble probe set from existing material datasets and rendered stimuli with known BSDF categories; evaluate transparent/mirror/glass models; build the 3x3 physical confusion matrix.
main_risk: Rendered stimuli realism; complement with curated real photos of known materials.
datasets: Trans10K, GDD, MSD, TROSD (public); rendered probes
survival_note: Keep; taxonomy work that seeds several follow-ups.

title: Persistence-latency frontier for fire/smoke alarms: temporal filtering trades detection delay against false alarms in a currently uncharacterized way.
problem: Known: deployed fire detection uses temporal persistence rules over per-frame model outputs; the frontier (delay vs false-alarm rate) is set ad hoc per deployment without published characterization.
hypothesis: The persistence-latency frontier has strongly diminishing returns beyond a few seconds of confirmation for most false-alarm types, but steam/fog confusers require an order of magnitude longer confirmation - the frontier is confuser-dependent, so single-threshold persistence is structurally suboptimal.
why_important: Detection delay is lives and acres in wildfire response; principled frontier curves would replace folklore thresholds across the industry.
why_novel: This operational layer is invisible in academic papers, which report frame-level metrics only.
minimal_experiment: On long wildfire-camera sequences with verified event times (FIgLib/HPWREN) plus confuser sequences, sweep persistence rules over frozen detectors; publish delay-vs-FAR frontiers stratified by confuser type.
main_risk: Event-time ground truth is noisy; needs careful verification protocol.
survival_note: Keep; operational science that practitioners will actually use.

title: Which rendering factor drives syn-to-real transfer for wildfire imagery: a factorial ablation of the M4SFWD generation pipeline.
problem: Known: M4SFWD demonstrates synthetic wildfire data helps detection, but which rendering choices (smoke turbulence model, lighting, terrain diversity, camera model) carry the transfer value is unknown - synthetic-data papers report the bundle, never the factors.
hypothesis: Transfer benefit is concentrated in one or two factors (predicted: smoke plume dynamics fidelity and lighting diversity), while terrain/texture diversity contributes marginally - measurable by re-rendering factorial subsets in the same UE5 pipeline.
why_important: Synthetic pipelines are expensive; factor attribution tells every synthetic-data builder where fidelity money goes.
why_novel: Factorial rendering ablations exist for driving scenes in limited form; wildfire/participating-media version does not.
minimal_experiment: Recreate an M4SFWD-style UE5 pipeline; render 2^4 factorial variants (turbulence x lighting x terrain x camera); train detectors per cell; evaluate on real smoke test sets (SmokeSeg/FIgLib-derived); ANOVA on transfer.
main_risk: Rendering engineering effort is large; factor definitions must be locked before rendering.
compute: 4 GPUs training + significant rendering compute, ~2-3 weeks
datasets: M4SFWD (reference), new renders, SmokeSeg/FIgLib real test (public)
survival_note: Expensive; only if a rendering engineer joins - otherwise park.

title: Seeing through smoke: object segmentation behind semi-transparent occluders degrades with opacity in a law-like way that restoration does not fix.
problem: Known: smoke partially occludes scene content; two strategies exist (dehaze-then-segment vs robust-segment); their comparative behavior as a function of physical opacity is uncharacterized.
hypothesis: Segmentation accuracy of background objects declines smoothly with smoke opacity following a transferable curve, and restoration preprocessing shifts but does not flatten the curve - beyond a critical opacity, restoration adds hallucination errors faster than it removes occlusion errors.
why_important: Firefighting robotics and disaster response need to know the operational opacity envelope, not average benchmark numbers.
why_novel: Opacity-parameterized evaluation with physical grounding is absent; smoke synthesis over labeled scenes makes it feasible.
minimal_experiment: Composite physically-parameterized smoke (varying transmission) over Cityscapes/COCO scenes; evaluate segmentation with/without SOTA dehazing; fit accuracy-vs-transmission curves; validate on real smoke-occluded footage subset.
main_risk: Synthetic smoke realism; validate curve shape on limited real data.
survival_note: Keep; produces an operational envelope, reusable design.

title: Thin transparent structure recall (glass edges, stems, rims) is near zero and invisible to region metrics: a probe-based audit.
problem: Known: wine-glass stems, glass shelf edges, and rims are thin structures where region metrics (IoU) barely register total failure; robot collision risk concentrates exactly there.
hypothesis: Current transparent-object models have order-of-magnitude worse recall on thin glass substructures than on glass bodies, and IoU differences between SOTA models are uncorrelated with thin-structure recall - the benchmark metric cannot see the safety-relevant errors.
why_important: Grasping/collision incidents involve rims and stems; metric blindness means model selection ignores the deployment risk.
why_novel: Thin-structure-stratified evaluation exists for vessels in medical; nobody has ported the audit to transparent objects.
minimal_experiment: Annotate thin-substructure subsets in Trans10K/TROSD test sets (skeleton-based tagging); compute stratified recall for 6 models; correlate with headline IoU.
main_risk: Thin-structure annotation is tedious; skeleton-based semi-automatic tagging mitigates.
survival_note: Keep; cheap, safety-framed, feeds B11.

title: Wet-surface versus standing-water ambiguity: puddle segmentation fails on reflectance-only evidence and no dataset separates the classes.
problem: Known: puddles (traversable hazard) and wet asphalt (mostly benign) share specular appearance; existing water-hazard data (e.g., Puddle-1000) labels water regions without the wet-vs-standing distinction that driving decisions need.
hypothesis: Models trained on existing water-hazard labels conflate wet surfaces and standing water at high rates (measurable on a re-annotated probe set), and the distinction is recoverable from polarization or stereo but not from monocular RGB - defining a sensor requirement, not a modeling gap.
why_important: Autonomous driving in rain hinges on this distinction; misclassification in either direction is costly (phantom braking vs hydroplaning risk).
why_novel: The wet-vs-standing distinction has not been formalized as a benchmark or measured as a confusion mode.
minimal_experiment: Re-annotate water regions in existing driving datasets (Puddle-1000, rainy BDD100K frames) with wet/standing labels using temporal/context cues; measure model confusion; small polarization-camera capture for the sensor claim.
main_risk: Ground truth for the distinction is hard even for humans from stills; may need video-based adjudication.
datasets: Puddle-1000, BDD100K rainy subsets (public); small new captures
survival_note: Keep; concrete AV-safety framing.

title: Kitchen steam as the dominant domestic false-alarm class: a home-robotics probe set for participating-media discrimination.
problem: Known: home robots and cameras encounter steam (kettles, showers, cooking) daily; fire/smoke models are trained on outdoor/industrial smoke; the domestic confuser distribution is unrepresented.
hypothesis: Smoke models fire on kitchen steam at rates far above outdoor fog confusion (steam shares turbulent motion with smoke, removing the motion cue that separates fog), making steam the hardest domestic confuser - a prediction that inverts the outdoor difficulty ordering of 0436.
why_important: Domestic false alarms determine consumer product viability; the confuser ordering flip is scientifically interesting (cue-dependence of confusion).
why_novel: No domestic steam/smoke discrimination study or probe set exists.
minimal_experiment: Collect/curate labeled steam clips (cooking videos, bathroom scenarios) plus indoor smoke footage; evaluate smoke models; compare confusion orderings with outdoor confusers under matched motion statistics.
main_risk: Curation labor; indoor smoke footage with verified labels is scarce.
datasets: Curated video (YouTube-sourced with licenses), D-Fire indoor subset (public)
survival_note: Keep as companion to 0436/0437; consumer relevance.

title: RGB-thermal misregistration dominates fusion error in aerial fire mapping: an error-budget analysis for FLAME-style data.
problem: Known: UAV fire datasets (FLAME) pair RGB and thermal; fusion models assume alignment, but parallax, rolling shutter, and gimbal timing misalign modalities dynamically.
hypothesis: In RGB-thermal fire segmentation fusion, misregistration accounts for a larger share of the error budget than either modality's intrinsic segmentation error, and fusion gains reported in the literature shrink or invert when evaluated on registration-audited subsets.
why_important: If alignment is the binding constraint, engineering effort belongs in calibration/synchronization, not fusion architectures - a redirect for a growing subfield.
why_novel: Fusion papers acknowledge registration en passant; a quantified error-budget decomposition for aerial fire data does not exist.
minimal_experiment: Estimate per-frame RGB-thermal misregistration on FLAME sequences (mutual-information alignment); stratify fusion-model performance by misregistration magnitude; simulate controlled misalignment for dose-response.
main_risk: Ground-truth registration is itself estimated; use synthetic-misalignment arm for internal validity.
survival_note: Keep; classic error-budget science applied where nobody has.

title: Temporal label flicker in video-derived smoke datasets: frame-independent annotation creates inconsistent supervision that models inherit.
problem: Known: smoke datasets annotate frames independently even when sourced from video; the same plume gets different extents across adjacent frames, injecting high-frequency label noise with temporal structure.
hypothesis: Label flicker (frame-to-frame GT inconsistency beyond scene change) is measurable and large in video-derived smoke data, and models trained on it exhibit corresponding prediction flicker that temporal smoothing of labels (not predictions) removes - supervision inconsistency, not model instability, causes output flicker.
why_important: Prediction flicker drives false alarms through persistence filters (ties 0446); attributing it to labels changes the fix from post-processing to dataset repair.
why_novel: Label temporal-consistency audits have not been performed on smoke (or most video-derived segmentation) datasets.
minimal_experiment: Identify video-derived frame clusters in SMOKE5K/SmokeSeg; quantify GT flicker via optical-flow-warped label agreement; train on original vs temporally reconciled labels; compare prediction flicker and accuracy.
main_risk: Optical flow through smoke is unreliable; restrict flicker measurement to background-stable sequences.
survival_note: Keep; connects dataset failure (B12) to deployment behavior.

title: Segmentation quality does not predict grasp success for transparent objects: a task-grounded external validity test.
problem: Known: transparent-object perception is motivated by robotic grasping, but perception papers report mask metrics while grasping papers report success rates; the linking function is unmeasured.
hypothesis: Across perception models, mask IoU on transparent objects correlates poorly with downstream grasp success (which depends on rim/contact-edge accuracy and depth completion quality), and a rim-weighted metric predicts grasping far better - the field optimizes a metric misaligned with its own motivation.
why_important: Would redefine evaluation for transparent perception around task-relevant geometry, affecting all Trans10K/TransCG-style work.
why_novel: Task-grounded metric validation (perception metric vs manipulation outcome) has not been run for transparency.
minimal_experiment: In simulation (Isaac/PyBullet with refractive rendering) plus a small real-robot arm setup with TransCG objects: sweep perception models, execute standardized grasps, correlate metric families with success.
main_risk: Sim-to-real of refraction; the real-robot arm requires lab access - simulation-only version is a weaker but publishable start.
survival_note: High-value if robotics infrastructure exists; else run sim-only variant.

title: Multispectral sufficiency for satellite smoke mapping: which bands beyond RGB actually carry the smoke signal.
problem: Known: satellite products flag smoke using multispectral heuristics; deep models increasingly use RGB composites for accessibility; the marginal value of each spectral band for smoke delineation is not cleanly measured.
hypothesis: A band-ablation study on Sentinel-2/Landsat scenes with verified smoke plumes shows the aerosol-sensitive short bands contribute the majority of separability from cloud, and RGB-only smoke mapping has a hard ceiling well below multispectral performance - quantifying an accessibility-accuracy tradeoff.
why_important: Determines whether cheap RGB-based wildfire monitoring (public web imagery, small sats) can ever match agency products.
why_novel: Band importance is folklore in remote sensing; a controlled ablation with modern segmentation models and verified plume labels is not published to my knowledge.
minimal_experiment: Assemble Sentinel-2 scenes with plume annotations (derived from active-fire products + manual QC); train matched models on band subsets; report separability and boundary quality per subset.
main_risk: Plume GT derivation circularity (products themselves use bands); manual annotation of a subset controls this.
survival_note: Keep; clean information-value study.

title: Amodal extent of transparent objects is ill-defined: annotation ambiguity between visible-region and physical-extent conventions.
problem: Known: for opaque objects, visible vs amodal masks differ by occlusion; for transparent objects the 'visible' region is itself paradoxical (you see through it), and datasets silently mix conventions.
hypothesis: Instructing annotators under explicit visible-appearance vs physical-extent conventions yields systematically different masks for the same transparent objects (differences concentrated at faint edges and interior holes), and existing datasets are measurably inconsistent mixtures of the two conventions.
why_important: Convention mixing caps achievable performance and corrupts cross-dataset comparisons - foundational hygiene for the subfield.
why_novel: Amodal-vs-visible is studied for occlusion; the transparency-specific version of the ambiguity has not been articulated or measured.
minimal_experiment: Dual-convention re-annotation of 150 Trans10K/GDD images; quantify convention gap; classify existing GT masks by nearest convention to expose dataset mixing.
main_risk: Small-scale annotation; the finding is definitional and might be dismissed without a downstream impact demo - add a training-outcome arm.
compute: Annotation-centric; 1 GPU for the training arm
datasets: Trans10K, GDD, GSD (public); new dual annotations
survival_note: Keep; definitional groundwork enabling 0434/0449.

title: Do camouflage-breaking skills transfer? COD-trained models as zero-shot detectors of isointense lesions and low-contrast targets.
problem: Known: camouflaged-object detection and low-contrast medical lesion detection share the abstract problem (target statistically similar to surround), but the communities never test transfer, so whether 'camouflage-breaking' is a generalizable skill is unknown.
hypothesis: COD-trained models transfer above generic-segmentation baselines to isointense targets in other domains (isointense brain lesions, sonar/thermal targets) only when the camouflage mechanism matches (texture similarity vs contour disruption) - transfer is mechanism-specific, not task-general, supporting a decomposition of 'camouflage' into named mechanisms.
why_important: Establishes whether COD is a fundamental capability worth investing in or a dataset-specific niche; the mechanism taxonomy would organize the field.
why_novel: Mechanism-stratified cross-domain transfer of COD has not been tested; 'apply COD model to X' papers exist but without the mechanism decomposition that makes it science.
minimal_experiment: Categorize COD10K test cases by camouflage mechanism; evaluate COD models zero-shot on matched-mechanism probes (isointense MS lesions from MSSEG, low-contrast targets in thermal/sonar public sets); test the mechanism-match interaction.
main_risk: Mechanism labeling is subjective; needs multiple raters and pre-registered definitions.
datasets: COD10K, CAMO, MSSEG, FLIR ADAS, public sonar sets (public)
survival_note: Keep; the mechanism-interaction design elevates it above naive transfer papers.

title: Refraction distortion fields as an unused transparency cue: do models exploit background warping at all?
problem: Known: refractive objects warp background texture in a physically constrained way; whether trained transparent-object models use this cue (versus specular highlights and context) is unknown.
hypothesis: Probing with warp-neutralized counterfactuals (synthetically removing refraction distortion while preserving color/specular content) leaves model predictions nearly unchanged - current models ignore refraction, leaving a physically reliable cue on the table; humans degrade substantially under the same manipulation.
why_important: Identifies a concrete perceptual gap between human and machine transparency perception, and a cue whose exploitation would generalize (physics, not dataset statistics).
why_novel: Cue-ablation psychophysics compared directly against model probing has not been done for refraction.
minimal_experiment: Render paired scenes (with/without refractive warping, keeping Fresnel effects) in Blender; evaluate Trans10K-trained models and human raters on both; compare cue sensitivity.
main_risk: Synthetic-to-real gap of the probe stimuli; supplement with real thin-glass vs patterned-background photo pairs.
survival_note: Keep; mechanistic cue analysis with human comparison.

title: Participating-media unification: fog density estimation, smoke segmentation, and underwater turbidity as one task family with transferable representations.
problem: Known: fog (driving), smoke (fire), and turbidity (underwater) are all scattering-media perception problems handled by disjoint literatures with incompatible labels (masks vs density vs restoration targets).
hypothesis: Models trained on physically parameterized transmission estimation in one medium transfer to the others far better than mask-trained models do, evidencing a shared 'scattering perception' representation and supporting a unified task formulation. (Speculation: a single transmission-pretrained backbone could serve all three communities.)
why_important: Unification would pool three small literatures' data and let progress compound instead of fragmenting.
why_novel: The three fields cite different ancestors (dehazing, fire, marine robotics); no cross-media transfer study exists.
minimal_experiment: Train transmission estimators on synthetic fog (physics-based over Cityscapes) and evaluate zero-shot transmission/extent estimation on SMOKE5K smoke and underwater datasets (SUIM); compare against mask-trained transfer.
main_risk: Physical differences (aerosol phase functions) may break transfer - which would itself map the family structure.
survival_note: High-concept; keep as unifying-theory candidate.

title: Smoke plume source localization from segmentation output: masks are insufficient for the one geometric question responders ask.
problem: Known: wildfire response needs the plume origin (ground point); segmentation masks delineate the visible plume, whose base is often occluded or below the horizon line of the camera.
hypothesis: Source localization error derived from mask geometry alone is dominated by base-occlusion and wind-advection effects and does not improve with mask quality beyond a modest threshold - the operationally relevant quantity requires temporal and multi-view reasoning that mask-centric research cannot deliver.
why_important: Redefines the smoke-vision objective around the decision-relevant output (origin geolocation) rather than pixels; changes what datasets should record (camera pose, multi-view).
why_novel: The mask-to-source insufficiency has not been quantified; multi-camera triangulation archives (HPWREN) make it testable.
minimal_experiment: On multi-camera wildfire archives with known fire origins (incident reports), compute source estimates from single-view masks vs multi-view triangulation; regress localization error on mask quality to show the plateau.
main_risk: Ground-truth origins from incident data are coarse; sample size of well-documented multi-view events is limited.
datasets: HPWREN camera archives, FIgLib, incident report metadata (public)
survival_note: Keep; task-redefinition studies have outsized influence.

title: Nighttime fire segmentation is exposure-information-limited: quantify the recoverable signal with HDR bracketing.
problem: Known: night fire scenes span extreme dynamic range (saturated flame vs black surroundings); single-exposure footage clips both ends; models are blamed for failures that may be pure information loss.
hypothesis: On matched night scenes, models given HDR (or exposure-bracketed) input recover a large, quantifiable fraction of the fire-extent error observed with auto-exposed input - establishing how much 'night failure' is sensor-side and setting an upper bound for software-only fixes.
why_important: Separates camera-procurement fixes from ML fixes for night wildfire monitoring, where most detections matter (fires grow overnight).
why_novel: Exposure-conditioned error decomposition for night fire has not been published; ties to 0433's emissive-photometry critique.
minimal_experiment: Capture/collect bracketed night fire footage (controlled burns, public HDR sets); evaluate models on single-exposure vs merged-HDR versions; decompose error into clipped-signal vs model components.
main_risk: Data collection; simulated clipping of HDR sources is a valid internal-control arm.
datasets: FLAME (some night), curated HDR footage; D-Fire night subset (public)
survival_note: Keep; complements 0433, cheap with synthetic-clipping arm.

title: Cross-dataset smoke label conventions disagree on where faint smoke ends: measure convention offsets among SMOKE5K, SmokeSeg, and detection-derived sets.
problem: Known: smoke datasets annotate 'smoke extent' with different implicit opacity thresholds (core plume vs faintest visible haze); cross-dataset training/evaluation mixes these conventions blindly.
hypothesis: Convention offsets between smoke datasets are measurable as systematic differences in the local-contrast level at which GT boundaries sit, and cross-dataset evaluation penalties correlate with the offset magnitude - a large share of 'generalization gap' between smoke datasets is threshold-convention mismatch.
why_important: Parallels medical convention findings (0389/0421) in a totally different domain, supporting a general theory that label-space shift masquerades as image-space shift.
why_novel: No cross-dataset convention audit exists for smoke; the contrast-at-boundary statistic is a new instrument for it.
minimal_experiment: Compute boundary-contrast distributions for GT in SMOKE5K/SmokeSeg/M4SFWD-seg-subsets; estimate per-dataset implicit thresholds; test correlation between threshold gaps and cross-dataset transfer losses of fixed models.
main_risk: Contrast statistic conflates plume physics with convention; normalize within scene types.
survival_note: Strong; cheap and theoretically load-bearing for the cluster.

title: Insect swarms, dust devils, and birds: transient biological/atmospheric confusers cause a distinct temporal false-alarm class no dataset covers.
problem: Known: long-horizon wildfire cameras record swarms, dust devils, and bird flocks that share transient, semi-transparent, moving-blob appearance with smoke; deployed systems reportedly suffer from them, but no labeled corpus exists.
hypothesis: Transient confusers cause false alarms with temporal signatures (duration, growth-rate, coherence) that separate them from smoke with simple spatiotemporal statistics - implying the false-alarm problem is solvable with temporal features that current single-frame models cannot access. (Hypothesis: growth-rate alone separates smoke from all transient confusers at high AUC.)
why_important: Provides the missing negative-class taxonomy for camera-network deployments and a falsifiable claim about which cue closes it.
why_novel: No public transient-confuser corpus or temporal-signature analysis exists for wildfire cameras.
minimal_experiment: Mine HPWREN archives for confirmed false-alarm clips (network operators log them) plus verified smoke; extract spatiotemporal statistics; test separability and augment a frozen detector with the top statistic.
main_risk: Access to operator false-alarm logs; without them, confuser mining is manual.
survival_note: Keep if log access secured; the taxonomy alone is a contribution.

title: Glass in the wild at night: retroreflections and interior lighting invert every daytime glass cue, and no benchmark measures it.
problem: Known: glass benchmarks (GDD/GSD/Trans10K) are overwhelmingly daytime/indoor-lit; at night, glass shows strong reflections of interior lights, headlight retroreflections, and darkness behind - cue structure inverts.
hypothesis: Daytime-trained glass models degrade catastrophically on night glass scenes (drop exceeding half their daytime margin over baseline), and the failure is cue-inversion rather than low light: relighting-normalized inputs do not recover performance. (Falsifiable via low-light-enhancement control arm.)
why_important: Night operation is mandatory for delivery robots and AVs; an unmeasured regime with inverted cues is a silent deployment hazard.
why_novel: No night-glass evaluation exists; the cue-inversion vs low-light decomposition (enhancement control) makes it a mechanism study, not just a robustness report.
minimal_experiment: Curate night glass probe set (storefronts, bus shelters) with annotation; evaluate SOTA glass models raw and after low-light enhancement; compare degradation attribution.
main_risk: Curation/annotation cost; nighttime annotation is genuinely harder - measure annotator agreement too.
datasets: GDD, GSD models; new night probe set; ExDark for enhancement baselines (public)
survival_note: Keep; fills an obvious hole with a mechanism question attached.

title: Soft-boundary supervision for ambiguous classes changes ranking but not means: testing whether the field's hard-mask habit hides real model differences.
problem: Known: for smoke/camouflage/translucency, some models may represent graded extent internally but are forced through hard-mask training/eval; whether soft (graded) supervision and evaluation would re-rank models is untested.
hypothesis: Training and evaluating the same architectures with soft targets (multi-annotator frequency maps or opacity proxies) changes model rankings substantially relative to hard-mask protocol (rank correlation < 0.6) while average scores move little - the field's protocol choice, not modeling, determines leaderboards in ambiguous domains.
why_important: A protocol-dependence result of this size would force ambiguous-object benchmarks to justify their target semantics - affecting smoke, COD, matting-adjacent tasks at once.
why_novel: Soft supervision is studied for calibration; its effect on model ranking in ambiguous-boundary domains has not been isolated.
minimal_experiment: On SMOKE5K (with 0431's multi-annotator data) and COD10K subsets: train 6 architectures under hard vs soft targets; evaluate under both protocols; report the 2x2 ranking-correlation matrix.
main_risk: Depends on multi-annotator data from 0431; run after it.
survival_note: Keep as the capstone experiment of the ambiguity subtheme.
